summary: Full backend + frontend verification of the Web3 TLD showcase. Backend: 14/14 pytest cases pass (/api/, /api/prices with 15 TLD prices + 8 examples each, /api/name-preview, /api/name-preview-stream NDJSON with fresh + cached timing, /api/leads, /api/status). Frontend (Playwright, 1920x1080 and 390x844): search bug fix verified (15 TLDs returned, all buyUrls clean with no %22/quotes, all target=_blank), streaming speed verified (first live-resolved card 6.2s, all 15 in 20.4s for a brand-new uncached name), TLD filter chips confirmed above input and functional (16 chips), default examples view shows 15 cards x 8 priced rows (120 valid freename links, e.g. oil.worldtrade $4,999), aiwebtools.app branding correct in nav/footer/domain card, domain card click opens https://freename.io/discover/transfermoney?ref=olive-ears-obey in a new tab, mobile has no horizontal overflow. Two real UI defects found (buy-button label overflow, no mobile nav) plus items that could not be verified in the headless environment (H.264 video playback, sold/struck-through example rows).

minor.issue: Generator awaits exactly len(TLD_SLUGS) queue items; if any worker task were cancelled/killed before queue.put the response would hang until client timeout. check_name_on_tld currently swallows all exceptions so it is not reproducible today, but add a timeout/sentinel guard.

fetch_tld_examples uses the same 10 hard-coded keywords for every TLD, so all 15 example cards show the identical name list (oil/ai/pay/trade/crypto/robot/gold/bank) with identical prices - looks templated rather than curated.

Missing video returns HTTP 200 with index.html (SPA catch-all) instead of 404. Browsers reject it on MIME sniff so the /videos/hero-stock.mp4 fallback still wins, but relying on a 200+HTML response for source fallback is fragile; better to remove the hero-ai source until the file exists.

ui_bugs.issue: In the 5-column desktop grid (chapter-01 at 1920px) the 'Buy on Freename' label overflows its yellow button box (scrollWidth 90 vs clientWidth 72) and visibly spills past the button/card edge. Buy button is squeezed by the 3 share icons + copy button in the same flex row.

At 390px all nav links are hidden (md:flex / sm:inline-flex) - nav-link-free-ai-tools, nav-browse-button and all chapter links are invisible and there is no hamburger menu, so the required 'Free AI Tools' chip is unreachable on mobile.

Clicking the upper image area of the card (y~40px) is intercepted by the parent grid container because of the rotateX/rotateY transformPerspective hit-box offset (Playwright: 'grid ... intercepts pointer events'). Clicks on the card body/title work and open the correct new tab, so impact is limited to the top strip of the card.

integration_issues.issue: While the stream is in flight each card shows the seeded FROM_PRICES value (e.g. $9.98) which then jumps to the real live price (e.g. $29.98) once resolved - users can read a wrong price for up to ~20s. Consider showing a skeleton/'checking...' instead of a stale seed price.

issues: All 15 TLD cards list the same 8 keywords with the same prices, making the section feel duplicated
Meta text at text-white/30-35 ('Minted on ...', 'once, forever - tap card to buy') is very low contrast on #050505
The 'From $9.98 - once, forever - tap card to buy' line wraps onto 2-3 lines in narrow 5-column cards

action_items: Fix 'Buy on Freename' button label overflow in the 5-column desktop card grid (shrink text / allow wrap / give the button min-width and move share icons to their own row).
Add a mobile nav (hamburger or visible chip) so the 'Free AI Tools' aiwebtools.app link and chapter links are reachable below 768px.
Avoid showing seeded FROM_PRICES as the price while the live stream is still resolving (price flickers 9.98 -> 29.98).
Optionally drop the /videos/hero-ai.mp4 <source> until the file exists (SPA returns 200/HTML for it) and diversify example keywords per TLD.
critical_code_review_comments: name_preview_stream: guard the consumer loop with asyncio.wait_for / sentinel so a dead worker cannot hang the NDJSON response forever.
ClaimYourName.jsx (290 lines) mixes streaming logic, filter chips, examples grid and results grid - extract the stream hook and the two grids into separate modules for maintainability.
Duplicate buy-URL construction: buyFor() in ClaimYourName.jsx duplicates backend buy_url_for()/data/domains.js buyUrl() - centralize to avoid the quoting regression reappearing.
fetch_tld_examples loops 10 keywords x 15 TLDs sequentially per slug on every 30-min refresh (150+ upstream calls); consider gathering keywords concurrently under the existing semaphore.

success_rate.frontend: ~90% (all requested flows pass except mobile nav visibility + buy-button overflow; hero video playback and sold-row rendering unverifiable in this environment)

seed_data_creation: One TEST_qa_lead lead and one TEST_qa status check inserted via public API during tests (harmless, no delete endpoint exists).
test_credentials: None needed; /app/memory/test_credentials.md is empty (app has no auth).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite lives at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/backend_test.py -v). Verified live: 120 example rows all use https://freename.io/results?search=<fqdn>&ref=olive-ears-obey with target=_blank and no %22; fresh-name stream timing 6.2s first / 20.4s complete; cached stream <1s. NOT verifiable here: (a) hero video playback - Playwright's headless Chromium returns canPlayType('video/mp4; codecs=avc1') = '' so H.264 (hero-stock.mp4 is avc1) never decodes; currentSrc DOES correctly resolve to /videos/hero-stock.mp4 and no media error is raised, so the fallback chain works - re-verify in a Chrome with proprietary codecs or convert a copy to VP9/WebM for testability; (b) example-sold-* struck-through rows - Freename currently returns AVAILABLE for every example, so 0 sold rows exist; code path in ClaimYourName.jsx lines 185-198 looks correct but is untested at runtime.
rca_of_the_issue: Buy-button overflow: DomainCard's action row puts 3 share anchors + copy button + a flex-1 buy anchor in one row; at xl:grid-cols-5 the card is only ~281px wide, leaving ~72px for a two-word uppercase label with tracking-[0.15em], so the text (90px intrinsic) escapes the button box. Card-click interception: the article uses framer-motion rotateX/rotateY with transformPerspective 900, which offsets the browser hit-box from the painted box near the card top edge, so elementFromPoint there resolves to the parent grid.
